## Why visit

A distinctive way to explore local beer in November without assuming Torrside’s seasonal brewery bar will open. This independent bar occupies a restored cotton mill beside the River Goyt, with vaulted ceilings, stonework and industrial columns giving the room as much interest as the views outside. The current operator names dedicated lines for Torrside, Thornsett and Ossett, and offers homemade food. Make it a daylight New Mills excursion if the mill-and-river setting appeals. Its recent ownership change is a reason to confirm the current beer board and service, not to rely on old Shrub Club descriptions.

## Beer

October 2026 CAMRA entry records three cask handpumps and Torrside live beer in membrane kegs; operator confirms the named local brewery lines.

## Cider and perry

**Real-cider offering not established.** Older listings mention a cider handpump, but current evidence does not establish a qualifying real-cider selection.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Current operator advertises homemade meals and baked snacks using local produce, with menu and booking links.

## Plan the visit

New ownership in autumn 2026; operator and CAMRA differ on exact takeover month. Official contact page says closed Monday/Tuesday. Check service and choose a suitable walking route into the gorge.

**Getting there:** New Mills has Central and Newtown stations on different lines; choose the service and walking approach deliberately.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
